about.title: La Mirada Medical Malpractice Claims
about.longDescription: Medical malpractice cases in La Mirada often begin with confusion — a diagnosis missed, a surgery gone wrong, or a medication given at the wrong dose. Because La Mirada sits within Los Angeles County, residents often receive care across several hospital systems and outpatient clinics along corridors like Imperial Highway and Rosecrans Avenue, which can make it harder to track down full medical records when something goes wrong. California law sets specific rules for these claims, including strict notice requirements and deadlines that differ from a typical injury case. A poor result doesn't automatically mean a provider was negligent — proving malpractice usually requires a qualified medical expert to explain what should have happened. Our team reviews the details of your case and explains what steps, if any, make sense next.

whyChoose.title: What Matters in a California Medical Malpractice Case

items.title: Strict Filing Deadlines
items.desc: California generally allows one year from when you discover the harm, and no more than three years from the injury itself. Missing these windows can end a claim before it starts.

items.title: 90-Day Notice Requirement
items.desc: Before filing a lawsuit against a healthcare provider, California law typically requires sending a 90-day pre-suit notice. Our team can help make sure this step is handled correctly and on time.

items.title: Expert Review Is Usually Required
items.desc: Because a bad outcome alone isn't proof of negligence, a qualified medical expert almost always has to weigh in on whether the standard of care was met.

items.question: I had a bad outcome after surgery near La Mirada Boulevard — is that automatically malpractice?
items.answer: Not necessarily. California law requires showing that a provider's care fell below the accepted medical standard, not just that the result was disappointing. We can help determine whether an expert review supports a claim.

items.question: How long do I have to bring a claim in California?
items.answer: Generally, you have one year from when you discover the injury, but no more than three years from when it happened. There's also often a required 90-day notice before filing suit, so timing matters early on.

items.question: Is there a limit on what I can recover?
items.answer: California law caps non-economic damages in medical malpractice cases, though that cap adjusts upward each year under current rules. Economic losses like medical bills and lost income are handled separately. We can walk you through how this applies to your situation.
